diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying the divergence theorem over any subdomain $D \subset \Omega_{x,t}$ yields the boundary conservation statement

issues.failure_explanation: Integrability and an interior distributional equation do not define ordinary restrictions of U and F(U) to every boundary. For example, with F=0, changing the representative U=0 on a single time slice preserves the weak solution but changes the displayed boundary integral for a rectangle ending on that slice. Normal traces and an appropriate class of domains are required; the classical divergence theorem does not establish the asserted equivalence under the stated assumptions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a trace-qualified Gauss–Green formulation on Lipschitz control volumes, restricting the assertion to fields possessing the required normal traces, such as suitable BV states. Interpret face values as traces rather than arbitrary representatives.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed boundary formulation, including its entropy analogue, is not well-defined for the full class of integrable weak states described in the paper.
issues.title: Boundary-flux equivalence lacks the necessary trace hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial trace formulation or regularity restriction is needed. The intended BV shock applications can survive without changing the control-volume architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Boundary flux integrals are evaluated using Gauss-Legendre quadrature on each control-volume face with 6 points.

issues.failure_explanation: A fixed finite quadrature rule can miss a localized boundary feature between its nodes: a smooth bump supported between nodes has zero quadrature value but a positive integral. No uniform trace-regularity bound, adaptive quadrature criterion, or quadrature-error term is supplied for the sharpening neural profiles or discontinuous ansatz. Thus computed residuals are not certified approximations of the exact-integral losses used in the analysis.

failure_location.quote: The combination of multi-scale adaptive sampling and accurate deterministic quadrature ensures that the weak and entropy residuals are evaluated reliably throughout the entire space--time domain, including in regions containing shocks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the analysis as concerning exact boundary integrals and withdraw the unconditional fixed-Q reliability assertion. A guarantee for computed losses must additionally include controlled quadrature errors or a refinement condition making them vanish.
issues.overall_effect: Small implemented losses cannot, on the stated information, certify small exact boundary residuals, especially near shocks.
issues.title: Fixed quadrature does not guarantee reliable shock residuals
issues.why_classification: This requires a contained quadrature-error analysis or a substantive qualification of the computed-loss guarantee, but not a replacement of the underlying method.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated entropy inequality implies that the displayed test-function integral is nonnegative for admissible solutions, not nonpositive. Consequently E_R measures admissible entropy dissipation rather than its violation. A Burgers shock from 1 to 0 has zero conservation loss and zero positive-part entropy loss, but strictly positive R_{k,φ} for suitable 0<k<1 and φ. Conversely, an expansion shock has E_R=0, so this quantity also cannot support the cited entropy-solution error estimate. The proof's absolute entropy residuals cannot be substituted by a loss that discards precisely these negative production terms.

failure_location.quote: For any partition $\{D_i\}_{i=1}^{N_D}$ of $\Omega \times (0,T)$, the continuous weak truncation error is bounded by the volume-weighted network losses:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the violation quantity using the supremum of minus R_{k,φ}, and consistently use positive entropy production, rather than absolute entropy production, in its subsequent bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete-to-continuous entropy bound and the later interpretation of E_R as an admissibility defect use the wrong orientation.
issues.title: The truncation error has the entropy sign reversed
issues.why_classification: The correct orientation is directly determined by the paper's entropy inequality. This local correction preserves the intended admissibility criterion; the separate quantitative and stability defects are inventoried independently.

issues.failure_explanation: The implemented entropy loss uses one fixed pair, whereas E_R takes a supremum over every Kružkov entropy |u-k|. No bound connecting these different residuals is established. This is substantive for the allowed general fluxes: for F(u)=u^3, the jump from -1 to 1 moving at speed 1 conserves both u and the strictly convex entropy η=u²/2, whose compatible flux is 3u⁴/4. Nevertheless its Kružkov entropy production is 2k(1-k²)>0 for 0<k<1. Thus the fixed-pair losses can vanish on a nonentropy weak solution.

failure_location.quote: corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the fixed scalar entropy penalty by a loss controlling the full Kružkov family, for example a supremum over k of the corresponding positive-part control-volume losses, and make the entropy-selection claims conditional on that family.
issues.overall_effect: The proof assumes entropy constraints absent from the loss, and the general scalar entropy-selection guarantee is unsupported even after correcting the sign of E_R.
issues.title: One entropy pair does not control the required Kružkov family
issues.why_classification: A new but contained family of entropy constraints is required. The same neural and control-volume architecture can remain, without restricting the analysis to a fundamentally different solver.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals

issues.failure_explanation: Integration by parts with a nonconstant φ produces weighted boundary terms and interior distributional terms, not unweighted net fluxes. Interior cancellations are invisible to the proposed right-hand side. For a single rectangular control volume, take F=0, u0=0, τ=t/T and Nθ(t)=tanh(t-T). Then Uθ vanishes on both time faces, so every conservation and entropy net flux is zero, but its nonconstant time dependence gives a nonzero test-function residual. This counterexample is a smooth instance of the paper's own ansatz and survives correcting the entropy sign and family.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must control unresolved within-cell residuals through additional test moments, a stronger residual norm, or a proved refinement/localization estimate with the necessary regularity and error terms.
issues.overall_effect: The central lemma does not link the proposed finite control-volume losses to the continuous weak defect, so the convergence proof loses its principal bridge.
issues.title: Net cell fluxes cannot bound arbitrary test-function residuals
issues.why_classification: The claimed estimate is false even for a smooth one-cell example. Repairing it requires a substantially different discrete-to-continuous argument or stronger loss information.

issues.failure_explanation: The first factor in the Cauchy–Schwarz bound is sqrt(N_D L_cons), not sqrt(L_cons); the same normalization problem affects the entropy term. It is not harmless under refinement: a constant residual density r gives R_i=r|D_i| and L_cons=r²|Ω×(0,T)|/N_D, tending to zero solely because the partition has more cells.

failure_location.quote: Recognizing that $\sum |D_i| = |\Omega \times (0,T)|$ and substituting the definitions of $L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)$ and $L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)$ defined in Section 3, we obtain the upper bound for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use summed volume-normalized losses, with consistent objective weighting, or retain the missing sqrt(N_D) factors and require N_D L_cons and N_D L_ent to vanish whenever N_D varies.
issues.overall_effect: The partition-uniform loss bound and its convergence interpretation omit an essential dependence on the number of control volumes.
issues.title: The loss-to-residual estimate drops the averaging factor
issues.why_classification: A contained renormalization or N_D-dependent weakening is available, but the unrestricted loss-to-zero criterion cannot be preserved by merely changing a numerical constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When a boundary face of a control volume $D_k$ coincides with the physical boundary of the domain $\Omega_x$, the flux integration across this face directly enforces the prescribed boundary conditions naturally through the evaluation of $R_\theta(D_k)$.

\State \textbf{Input:} initial condition  $U_0$, flux $F(U)$, entropy pair $(\eta,q)$,
domain $\Omega_{x,t}$, loss weights $\lambda_1 = 1,\lambda_2=1,\lambda_{\mathrm{TVD}}=1$

issues.failure_explanation: On a bounded domain, interior residuals and initial data do not control incoming boundary information. For F(u)=u on (0,1), u=x-t and v=x-t+g(t-x), with smooth g vanishing for nonpositive arguments, have the same initial data, bounded spatial variation and zero interior entropy defects, but different terminal states. Evaluating F(Uθ) on a physical boundary imposes no prescribed boundary data because none enter the residual or algorithm.

failure_location.quote: Let $u$ be the unique entropy solution of \eqref{eq:conservation_law} with initial condition $u_0 \in L^\infty(\Omega) \cap BV(\Omega)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, prescribe an admissible boundary problem, enforce the corresponding boundary data, and supply a stability estimate including boundary discrepancies or matching-boundary hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted initial-data-only error estimate, uniqueness conclusion and natural boundary-enforcement claim fail for the finite-domain problems covered by the paper.
issues.title: The stability theorem and method omit boundary-data control
issues.why_classification: The missing information allows different exact solutions with identical stated losses and initial data. Restoring the finite-domain guarantee requires additional boundary enforcement and stability theory, not a local constant correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines TV by an ordinary gradient integral even though its ansatz retains discontinuities of U0. For the stated step initial data and Nθ=0, the almost-everywhere spatial gradient is zero, whereas the actual BV variation is |1-τ(t)| times the initial jump. Thus the defined quantity is not the BV seminorm required by the stability theorem and does not measure the asserted variation bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the distributional variation |D_x Uθ|(Ω). For the stated ansatz, include the singular contribution inherited from (1-τ)D_xU0, or explicitly account for its known bound when defining M.
issues.overall_effect: The TV hypothesis and regularization are identified with the wrong quantity for the discontinuous data used throughout the experiments.
issues.title: The defined TV seminorm omits singular BV variation
issues.why_classification: The initial data are already assumed BV, so incorporating their fixed singular variation is a standard local correction that preserves the intended regime and rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The test functions cannot detect terminal layers uniformly. Take F=0, Ω=(0,1), u0(x)=x and vδ(x,t)=x+aχδ(t), where χδ is smooth, zero until T-δ and equals one at T. Both spatial variations equal one, and the initial error is zero. Since |u-k| is 1-Lipschitz, E_R(vδ)≤aδ, for either entropy-sign convention, while the terminal L1 error is a. The asserted bound tends to zero. Mere measurability also leaves endpoint values unconstrained, but even time continuity does not repair this example.

failure_location.quote: \|v(\cdot, T) - u(\cdot, T)\|_{L^1(\Omega)} \leq \|v(\cdot, 0) - u_0\|_{L^1(\Omega)} + C \sqrt{TV(u_0) \cdot \sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(v(\cdot, t)) \cdot \sqrt{E_R(v)}},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, introduce residual information reaching the time boundary or suitable uniform temporal control, define endpoint traces, and prove a stability estimate for that strengthened setting.
issues.overall_effect: The quoted stability theorem cannot turn the defined interior dual quantity into the claimed fixed-terminal-time estimate.
issues.title: The interior weak defect cannot control terminal-time error
issues.why_classification: A uniformly bounded, smooth, nondegenerate-BV counterexample defeats the estimate. The missing endpoint control requires a different stability argument or a substantially stronger approximation hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: For F=0, u0=0 and v(x,t)=t, all stated hypotheses hold and the initial error is zero. Both spatial variations vanish, so the asserted right-hand side is zero despite terminal error T|Ω| and a nonzero finite residual. This is not repaired by merely excluding zero variation: u0=εx and v=εx+t give positive variations tending to zero while the terminal error remains fixed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the displayed formula by a valid entropy-stability estimate that also controls spatially constant residual modes and includes the necessary consistency terms.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Bouchut–Perthame estimate is false even without shocks, boundary effects or problematic endpoint representatives.
issues.title: The BV-product prefactor annihilates genuine approximation errors
issues.why_classification: The prefactor suppresses an entire legitimate class of errors, including nearby nondegenerate cases. A valid replacement stability result, with potentially different rates, is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Sample space--time subdomains $\{D_k\}_{k=1}^{N_D}$ at multiple scales.
the method penalizes violations of the weak conservation identity and the entropy inequality over a collection of dynamically sampled space--time control volumes.

issues.failure_explanation: The only stated loss-to-defect lemma assumes a partition, including exact coverage and the identity sum |D_i|=|Ω×(0,T)|. The main theorem imposes no such hypothesis and uses losses from arbitrary dynamically sampled volumes. Overlap, uncovered regions and changing sample sets are not addressed. Even a valid partition estimate would not justify this application; finite sampled losses can miss modifications outside the tested regions.

failure_location.quote: From Lemma 1, the continuous entropy defect is bounded by the network losses:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, prove a coverage/generalization estimate for the actual sampling scheme and specify its deterministic or probabilistic hypotheses. Restricting the theorem to suitable partitions would withdraw the advertised sampled-volume guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The formal convergence claim does not cover the advertised mesh-free sampling procedure on its stated assumptions.
issues.title: The main theorem applies a partition result to sampled overlapping volumes
issues.why_classification: The gap concerns the central passage from the implemented sampling regime to a global error guarantee and requires new sampling theory or exclusion of that regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding expression is C sqrt(TV(u0)M) E_R^(1/4), not a multiple of E_R^(1/2). Substituting the stated lemma therefore gives a volume factor |Ω×(0,T)|^(1/8) and loss powers L_cons^(1/8)+L_ent^(1/8). The displayed replacement by a square root yields a stronger bound that does not follow for small losses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Downgrade the derived rate to 1/8, correct the constant, and revise the associated rate claims. Retaining 1/4 would require a stronger stability estimate not supplied in the source.
issues.overall_effect: Even granting the other estimates, the advertised explicit 1/4 loss-to-L1 rate and its stated constant are not derived.
issues.title: The substitution changes an eighth-power loss rate into a quarter-power rate
issues.why_classification: The source-supported algebraic repair materially worsens the paper's central quantitative convergence rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The conserved variables are approximated directly by a neural network
The system is strictly hyperbolic for $h>0$

issues.failure_explanation: No output constraint or update invariant enforces positive depth, positive density or positive internal energy. Allowed network outputs can therefore give h=0 or ρ=0, making velocities and conservative fluxes undefined, or p≤0, making the Euler entropy logarithm undefined. Positive initial data do not prevent this: the ansatz equals the unconstrained network at T and can leave the admissible state set earlier.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an admissible-state output construction, such as positive exponential outputs for h, ρ and p with Euler energy reconstructed from the stated equation of state, and choose 0≤τ≤1. Alternatively enforce equivalent admissibility constraints at every update and evaluation.
issues.overall_effect: The training procedure is not mathematically well-defined for all permitted initializations and updates in the Euler and shallow-water applications.
issues.title: Unconstrained network states can make physical fluxes and entropies undefined
issues.why_classification: A contained output parameterization or invariant is needed. It changes the executable construction but does not require a new global solver architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To guarantee this condition, we introduce a TVD regularization term:
The TVD regularization guarantees $\sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(U_\theta(\cdot, t)) \leq M$ for some constant $M$;

issues.failure_explanation: A finite sampled maximum and finite point differences do not bound the true space-time supremum of spatial variation. Smooth neural profiles can develop narrow high-variation peaks between sampled spatial points or sampled times while the reported penalty is arbitrarily small. Resampling alone supplies no uniform-in-θ certificate. Thus the implementation does not establish the uniform BV hypothesis used in the convergence statement.

failure_location.quote: Sample a random cloud of points and compute $L_{\mathrm{TVD}}$ as in Section~\ref{sec:tvd}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the sampled term as a heuristic regularizer and retain a separately verified true-BV bound as an explicit hypothesis, or replace it by a certified upper bound with appropriate uniform sampling control.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed automatic TV guarantee is unsupported; the main theorem's BV assumption remains an independent condition rather than a consequence of training.
issues.title: The sampled TV penalty does not certify a uniform BV bound
issues.why_classification: A genuine uniform-control argument or a substantive qualification of the training guarantee is required, while the conditional convergence framework can remain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This construction guarantees $U_\theta(x,0) \equiv U_0(x)$, eliminating the initial condition error term from the convergence analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated ansatz, Uθ(·,0)=U0 exactly for every θ. Consequently every defined initial-time error against the prescribed nonzero Burgers initial state must be zero, including errors evaluated on a finite grid. The repeated positive initial errors, also present for shallow-water depth, cannot describe that construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reconcile the implementation with the stated ansatz and regenerate the affected error reports. If a different initial-condition treatment was actually used, identify it explicitly and retain its initial-error contribution in comparisons with the theory.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical tables and the claimed implementation of exact initial enforcement are mutually inconsistent, so the experiments do not unambiguously validate the analyzed method.
issues.title: Reported initial errors contradict the hard initial-condition ansatz
issues.why_classification: Repeated quantitative results require implementation/reporting verification and potentially rerunning the experiments; this is not a single forced typographical correction.

issues.failure_explanation: At T=1 the ansatz is the continuous tanh network. The exact Burgers shock has a unit jump and L∞ norm one. Every continuous approximation has essential sup error at least half that jump, hence relative L∞ error at least 0.5. The reported 0.4649 violates this bound; the interaction test similarly reports 0.4423 at a unit jump. Finite test-point maxima may be smaller, but they are not the stated continuum norm errors.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the continuum supremum errors, or explicitly define and label the quantities as sampled maximum errors with their evaluation grid and limitations. Do not use them as continuum L∞ accuracy claims.
issues.overall_effect: The tabulated L∞ accuracy claims cannot be interpreted as actual continuum sup-norm errors for the stated approximation.
issues.title: Reported continuum sup-norm errors violate the jump lower bound
issues.why_classification: A meaningful quantitative metric claim must be corrected or weakened to a discrete diagnostic, although the method's L1 objectives need not change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: All experiments are performed on the domain $\Omega = [-1,1]$ with final time $T=1$.
This configuration produces a rarefaction wave at the left interface and a shock at the right interface.

issues.failure_explanation: Before interaction, the rarefaction's leading edge is x=-0.5+t and the shock is x=t/2. They first meet at t=1, exactly the reported final time. Thus the experiment reaches first contact but supplies no post-contact interval on which stability throughout the interaction or the altered shock evolution is tested.

failure_location.quote: The method remains stable throughout the interaction and accurately captures the change in solution topology.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the test as pre-interaction evolution up to first contact, or extend the computation beyond t=1 and validate the post-interaction solution.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed validation of the interacting-wave regime exceeds the time interval actually reported.
issues.title: The interaction experiment ends at first wave contact
issues.why_classification: A genuine limitation of the tested regime must be acknowledged or a new validation interval supplied; the numerical method itself need not be redesigned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \caption{Relative errors at different times for the shallow water (Stoker) problem.}

issues.failure_explanation: For an instantaneous relative velocity error at t=0, the exact reference velocity is identically zero, so its Lp norm is zero and the relative error is undefined. The paper supplies no zero-safe normalization for these entries. Its displayed space-time metric also does not itself define separate instantaneous errors. Consequently the finite positive initial-time values have no defined interpretation as the reported relative norms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Mark these relative errors as undefined, or report explicitly defined absolute errors or a separately stated nonzero normalization for the zero-reference case.
issues.overall_effect: The initial-time velocity diagnostics in the shallow-water table are mathematically undefined under the stated relative-error convention.
issues.title: Initial-time relative velocity errors have zero reference norm
issues.why_classification: This is a local degenerate-metric repair that leaves the nonzero-reference accuracy measurements and the method's guarantees unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For one-dimensional shallow water with m=hu, the proposed q is m³/(2h²)+ghm/2. Its derivative with respect to m is 3m²/(2h²)+gh/2, whereas the required component of ∇η DF is 3m²/(2h²)+gh. Thus compatibility fails for positive h. The correct vector energy flux is (η+gh²/2)u, not ηu.

failure_location.quote: In all cases, the entropy functions are convex and the corresponding entropy fluxes satisfy the compatibility condition with the physical flux, ensuring consistency with the entropy inequality.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the shallow-water entropy flux by q=(η+gh²/2)u in every dimension, then recompute or revalidate all shallow-water entropy residuals and experiments using that loss.
issues.overall_effect: The shallow-water entropy loss enforces the wrong inequality and can penalize smooth exact solutions; the stated physical-admissibility basis of those experiments is unreliable.
issues.title: The shallow-water entropy flux omits the pressure-work term
issues.why_classification: The correction is contained, but it changes an operational constraint used in the numerical method and requires revalidation rather than a purely typographical edit.
